title: Rotate a photo grid
prompt:
A square photo is stored as an n × n grid of pixel values. Rotate it 90 degrees clockwise, changing grid in place, and return grid. Do not build a second grid.

- n is between 1 and 200.
- Pixel values are integers between 0 and 255.
hints: After a clockwise turn, the old row r becomes the new column n − 1 − r.
Two simple in-place moves combine into a rotation: flip over the main diagonal, then mirror each row.
When transposing, only swap cells with c > r, or each pair is swapped back.

solution.explanation: Transposing swaps grid[r][c] with grid[c][r], turning rows into columns. Reversing each row then mirrors left and right. Together they send the cell at (r, c) to (c, n − 1 − r), which is exactly a 90 degree clockwise turn, and both steps work in place.

complexity.notes: Each cell is moved a constant number of times. Rotating ring by ring, four cells at a time, gives the same bounds with one pass.

followUps: Rotate ring by ring, moving four cells at a time.
